proposedTopics.title: Tries
proposedTopics.description: A tree specialized for prefix operations on strings; every trie problem is really a Trees:DFS traversal over children keyed by character.

proposedTopics.title: Trie construction & search
proposedTopics.description: Each node holds a map/array of child edges keyed by character plus an end-of-word flag; insert/search walk one character at a time. Recognize: repeated prefix queries, dictionary-style lookup.

proposedTopics.title: Word Search II / prefix matching
proposedTopics.description: Build a trie of the target words, then DFS the grid while walking the trie in lockstep, pruning branches with no matching prefix. Recognize: "find all words from a dictionary in a grid".

proposedTopics.title: Autocomplete applications
proposedTopics.description: Traverse to a prefix's node, then DFS the subtree to collect all completions (often ranked/limited). Recognize: "suggest completions for a prefix".

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for a trie instead of a hash set of words? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: repeated prefix queries ("does any word start with..."), dictionary-style lookup, autocomplete, shared-prefix storage where a hash set would rescan whole words. Pitfall: forgetting the end-of-word flag — without it "app" looks present just because "apple" was inserted, and prefix-search gets confused with full-word search.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the trie node plus insert and search in your language of choice: a node with a character-keyed children map and an end-of-word flag, insert walking/creating one node per character, search walking to confirm a full word.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Node = { children: char -> Node, isEnd: bool }. Insert: start at root, for each char descend into children[char], creating the child if absent; mark isEnd on the final node. Search: descend char by char, return false the moment a child is missing, else return the final node's isEnd. startsWith is the same walk without the isEnd check. Invariant: the path from root to any node spells exactly the prefix that node represents.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree) (Medium) — support insert(word), search(word), and startsWith(prefix).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: One node type with a children map and a boolean end flag; search and startsWith share the descend loop and differ only in whether the end flag must be true.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure (Medium) — addWord and a search where '.' matches any single character.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Store words in a trie; on '.' branch into a DFS/recursion that tries every child, otherwise follow the one matching child — the wildcard turns the linear walk into a small backtracking search.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you combine a trie with grid DFS instead of running a search per word? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "find all words from a dictionary in a grid/text", many target words sharing prefixes, where per-word search would rescan the board once per word. Pitfall: not pruning dead branches — walk the trie in lockstep with the DFS so a cell path with no matching trie child is abandoned immediately, and de-duplicate found words (or prune matched nodes) so the same word isn't reported twice. Related: Word Break II is the trie-accelerated segmentation variant (skipped here).

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Word Search II (Hard) — given a grid of letters and a word list, return every word that can be traced through adjacent cells.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Build a trie of the word list, then DFS each cell walking the trie in lockstep — the trie prunes every path whose prefix no target word shares, collapsing many per-word scans into one board traversal.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for a trie's prefix node as the anchor for completions or shortest-prefix lookup? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "suggest completions for a prefix", "replace a word by its shortest matching root/prefix", ranked/limited suggestions off a shared dictionary. Pitfall: re-walking from the root for every query instead of caching the prefix node, and (for shortest-prefix) not stopping at the FIRST end-of-word node on the descent. Related: Design Search Autocomplete System (premium, skipped here) adds ranking by historical frequency.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Replace Words (Medium) — given a dictionary of roots, replace each word in a sentence with the shortest root that is a prefix of it.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Insert all roots into a trie, then for each word descend character by character and stop at the first node flagged end-of-word — that shortest matching prefix is the replacement.
